messages.content: Calculate the area under the curve y=3x^2 + 2x - 4, between x = -1 and x = 2.

function.name: mathematics_calculate_area_under_curve
function.description: Calculate the area under the curve for a given polynomial function within a specified interval. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

polynomial.description: The coefficients of the polynomial, in decreasing order of exponent, where the first element is the coefficient for x^n, the second element is the coefficient for x^(n-1), and so on. The last element is the constant term.

limits.description: A list of two numbers specifying the lower and upper limit for the integration interval.

message.content:
**Solution**

The definite integral of  
\(f(x)=3x^{2}+2x-4\) from \(x=a\) to \(x=b\) gives the **signed** area under the curve:
\[
A_{\text{sig}}=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx .
\]

---

### Step 1 – Antiderivative  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\int \bigl(3x^{2}+2x-4\bigr)\,dx 
   &= x^{3}+x^{2}-4x + C .
\end{aligned}
\]

Call this primitive \(F(x)=x^{3}+x^{2}-4x\).

---

### Step 2 – Signed area from \(-1\) to \(2\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{\text{sig}}
    &=F(2)-F(-1)\\[4pt]
    &=\Bigl(2^{3}+2^{2}-4\cdot2\Bigr)
      -\Bigl((-1)^{3}+(-1)^{2}-4(-1)\Bigr) \\[4pt]
    &=\left(8+4-8\right)-( -1+1+4 )\\[4pt]
    &=4-4=0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Because the graph dips below the \(x\)-axis and later rises back up,
the positive and negative parts cancel each other out.

---

### Step 3 – Absolute (“true”) area

To obtain the actual geometric area we split the integral at the real root(s) of the quadratic.

Solve \(3x^{2}+2x-4=0\):
\[
x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{\,4+48\,}}{6}
  =\frac{-2\pm 2\sqrt{13}}{6}
  =\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{13}}{3}.
\]

Only the “positive” root lies inside our limits:
\[
r=\frac{\sqrt{13}-1}{3}\approx0.869 .
\]

Hence

\[
\text{True area}= \underbrace{\!\!-\!\!\int_{-1}^{\,r}(3x^{2}+2x-4)\,dx}_{\text{below }x\text{-axis}}
                 +\underbrace{\!\!\int_{\,r}^{\,2}(3x^{2}+2x-4)\,dx}_{\text{above }x\text{-axis}} .
\]

Using the antiderivative \(F(x)\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
I_1 &= -(F(r)-F(-1)) ,\\
I_2 &=  F(2)-F(r).
\end{aligned}
\]

Carrying out the algebra (exact form shown below) yields

\[
I_1 = I_2 = \frac{70+26\sqrt{13}}{27}\;\text{units}^2 .
\]

Adding them,

\[
\boxed{
\text{Total true area}
     = \frac{140+52\sqrt{13}}{27}
     \approx 12.1\;\text{square units}
}
\]

(The numerical approximation uses \(\sqrt{13}\approx3.606\).)

---

#### Summary

*Signed area*: \(0\)  
*Geometric (absolute) area*: approximately **12.1 square units**.
